title: Identifying an Active Promoter in B. saltans Using Luciferase Assay
author: Fatma Gomaa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sh5eb86

The PCR master mix (Master Mix 2 x NEB (Taq 2x))

steps.title: Measure plasmid concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the concentration of the luciferase plasmid using both a NanoDrop spectrophotometer and a Qubit fluorometer.

steps.title: Design primers with restriction sites
steps.instruction: Create forward and reverse PCR primers for the gene of interest that include the chosen restriction‑enzyme (RE) sequence at the 5′ end and add 3–4 extra nucleotides downstream of the RE site (these bases will be removed during digestion).

steps.title: Order cells and kits
steps.instruction: Order TOP‑10 chemically competent E. coli cells (e.g., “TOP‑10 10”) and acquire the required kits for restriction digestion, ligation, and gel purification.

steps.title: Amplify gene by PCR
steps.instruction: Perform PCR using 10–100 ng µl⁻¹ B. saltans genomic DNA as template, the designed primers (including RE sites), and amplify the target fragments (~0.6 kb and ~3 kb, one containing the putative ribosomal promoter).

steps.title: Verify PCR product on gel
steps.instruction: Run an aliquot of the PCR reaction on an agarose gel to confirm that the correct fragment size was amplified.

steps.title: Purify PCR product
steps.instruction: Purify the PCR product using a column‑based kit or magnetic beads, eluting in approximately 15 µl and obtaining a total volume of about 75 µl of purified DNA.

steps.title: Digest vector and insert
steps.instruction: In parallel, set up rapid restriction digests (max 3 h) for both the luciferase plasmid and the purified PCR product.

substeps.instruction: Take 750 ng of luciferase plasmid; add 1.5 µl of HindIII (10 U µl⁻¹); add water to bring the volume to ~17 µl.
Add the appropriate RE(s) to the PCR product in a similar total volume.

steps.title: Dephosphorylate vector
steps.instruction: After digestion, add 1/10 volume of Calf Alkaline Phosphatase (CAP) 10× buffer and 1 µl CAP enzyme to the plasmid digest, incubate 1 h at 37 °C, then heat‑inactivate at 65 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Run digested DNA on gel
steps.instruction: Mix each digest with loading buffer containing bromophenol blue and glycerol, load onto a 1 % agarose gel, and run alongside an undigested plasmid control. (The PCR‑product digest may be omitted from the gel if it will be purified directly.)

steps.title: Excise and freeze gel fragments
steps.instruction: Cut out the vector and insert bands with a sterile scalpel, place each fragment in a 1.5 ml tube, and freeze at –20 °C for at least 10 min (longer is fine).

steps.title: Gel‑fragment cleanup (Genelute)
steps.instruction: Purify the excised gel pieces using the Sigma Genelute kit.

substeps.instruction: Remove tubes from –20 °C and melt in a 56 °C heat block for 5–10 min.
Break the gel into the smallest possible pieces with a pipette tip or sterile spatula.
Add 100 µl TE buffer to the column, centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 s.
Transfer the column to a fresh collection tube, discard the old tube with TE.
Load the broken gel onto the column, ensuring fragments settle at the bottom.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 min.
Measure the eluate volume and add 1/10 volume of sterile 3 M sodium acetate.
Place the mixture at –20 °C overnight.

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation of DNA
steps.instruction: Recover the DNA by ethanol precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the –20 °C mixture for 10–20 min at maximum speed; discard the supernatant.
Add 200 µl 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 3 min at maximum speed, discard ethanol.
Briefly centrifuge 10 s, remove residual ethanol, and air‑dry the pellet for 10–15 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 15 µl TE buffer, incubate at room temperature for 30 min.
Pipette up/down to ensure complete dissolution, then run 1 µl of vector and 1 µl of insert on a gel for visualization and quantify with Qubit.

steps.title: Set up rapid ligation
steps.instruction: Ligate vector and insert using a rapid ligation protocol (max 2 h).

substeps.instruction: Use a vector‑to‑insert molar ratio of 1:5 (calculate with the Promega ratio calculator).
Add water (Z µl) to bring the total reaction volume to 10 µl.
Incubate at room temperature for 1–3 h without disturbance.

steps.title: Verify ligation by PCR (optional)
steps.instruction: Optionally amplify the ligation mix by PCR using the plasmid forward primer and the insert reverse primer to confirm successful insertion.

steps.title: Prepare competent cells for transformation
steps.instruction: Thaw TOP‑10 chemically competent cells on ice (keep on ice for 10 min). Keep the remainder of the ligation reaction at –20 °C in case a repeat is needed.

steps.title: Transform ligation into TOP‑10 cells
steps.instruction: Introduce the ligation mixture into the competent cells and perform heat shock.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µl ligation directly, or dilute 1 µl ligation to 5 µl and use 2.5 µl of that dilution.
Incubate on ice 10 min (if not already on ice).
Heat shock for 35 s in a 42 °C water bath.
Return tubes to ice for 2 min.
Add 210 µl SOC medium, shake at 37 °C for 1 h.

steps.title: Recover and plate transformed cells
steps.instruction: Plate the recovered cells on Miller’s LB agar containing ampicillin (50 µg ml⁻¹ or 100 µg ml⁻¹).

substeps.instruction: Spread the entire transformation volume over three plates.
Incubate plates overnight at 37 °C (no longer than 16 h).

steps.title: Store colonies and glycerol stocks
steps.instruction: Save a portion of each plate’s growth in glycerol stock for future use.

steps.title: Screen colonies by colony PCR
steps.instruction: Identify correct clones using colony PCR.

substeps.instruction: Prepare one 100 µl LB + ampicillin tube per planned PCR reaction.
Pick a white colony with a sterile toothpick, dip into PCR master mix, swirl, then transfer the same toothpick into the LB tube.
Repeat for all white colonies.
Run PCR with the plasmid forward primer and the gene‑of‑interest reverse primer.
Run the PCR products on an agarose gel to confirm the expected insert size and orientation.
Mark tubes that give a positive band.

steps.title: Grow positive colonies for plasmid prep
steps.instruction: Expand confirmed colonies in liquid culture.

substeps.instruction: Transfer LB from each positive tube into a 100 ml flask containing LB + ampicillin (make up to four 100 ml cultures).
Incubate overnight at 37 °C with shaking.

steps.title: Prepare plasmid DNA (Midi prep)
steps.instruction: Harvest the overnight cultures and isolate plasmid DNA using the Zymo Midi‑prep kit.

substeps.instruction: Elute plasmid in 200 µl buffer; expected concentration 200–300 ng µl⁻¹.
Quantify the eluted plasmid with Qubit.

steps.title: Confirm plasmid by sequencing PCR
steps.instruction: Perform a final PCR for sequencing using the provided primers and program.

substeps.instruction: Primers: Forward 8683‑8713 (CTGAAGCTTTGAAGGAAAGTCGAAACGCCGTGTGTGTG), Forward 6305‑6332 (CTGAAGCTTCGGTGTGTCGAGTGGAAGAAAGGACGAT), Reverse 9603‑9634 (ATCAAGCTTAGATTCCTGCAATGCAGTGATTCTGAGG).
PCR program: 95 °C 30 s; 95 °C 30 s; 61 °C 30 s; 68 °C 60 s; repeat steps 2‑4 for 29 cycles; 68 °C 5 min; hold at 10 °C.
Run at least 75 µl total PCR product (3 × 25 µl reactions) to obtain sufficient DNA for sequencing.
